title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization
layout_note: The two cases are stacked vertically, not side by side: the heterogeneous setting on top, the homogeneous setting below, separated by a grey dashed horizontal rule; each is a sketch of the same parameter space.
grouping: No containers; the dashed rule splits the two settings, each titled at its top right in plain serif text ('Heterogeneous setting', 'Homogeneous setting'). Marker shape and colour separate the kinds of point: blue triangles for the local optima, a green square for the global optimum, black dots for the start and server points.
shapes_depth: Flat vector sketch: a black dot for the shared start x^(t,0); solid blue arrow chains for each client's local steps (in the upper copy client 1's chain is much longer than client 2's); blue dashed arrows from the start to the averaged point; a red dashed line joining the clients' end points, with the server point x^(t+1,0) as a black dot on it. Bold italic math labels beside every point.
proposed_highlight: No method is shown; the two copies carry the argument: with unequal numbers of local steps (top) the averaged point lands far from the global optimum x*, with equal steps (bottom) close to it.
lesson: Show the bias of averaging unequal local progress by drawing the same parameter space twice, stacked - one client's step chain much longer in the upper copy - with the client end points joined by a red dashed line on which the server point sits, against fixed local and global optimum markers.
notes: Venue and year as recorded by Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); the arXiv v1 PDF names no venue. refs crop found no 'Figure 1' caption (the figure is wrapped beside body text), so page 2 was rendered at 200 dpi with pdftoppm and the figure cut out above its caption (crops/2007.07481/fig1.png in the federated kb-build work dir); pdfimages lists no embedded images on that page, so the crop's figN.json records images_px [] and photo_share is 0. elements 'other' = the optimum markers (triangles, square) in parameter space.
